pathBase: All image inputs and outputs are relative to this file.

stages.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Style: polished desktop website design, refined editorial magazine typography, quiet rigorous grid, unusually generous vertical breathing room. New serif typography must use regular/book weight; source logo typography stays faithful. Canvas white, graphite body text, subtle paper grain, no browser chrome, no viewport frame. Avoid pastel pink and pale blue fields, avoid duplicate brand emblems, avoid slogan clutter, oversized headings, full-page dark blocks, photos, city maps, phones and table views. Create a fresh composition, not a rearrangement of the earlier twin-logo design.
Asset type: landscape design sheet showing exactly two desktop header states, Software above and Consulting below, with ample blank page between them.
Primary request: radically clarify HERE versus THERE. Each header has exactly ONE complete current-site logo. The sibling website is a small ordinary outbound editorial text link, NOT a logo, NOT another masthead, NOT a repeated pinwheel mark. The asymmetry must be immediately obvious.
Input images: Image 1 is the original complete Sebastian/Software lockup; Image 2 is the original complete Sebastian/Consulting lockup. Use each only for the current identity of its own corresponding header. Remove the input background swatches; reproduce the original emblem and full Sebastian/slash/suffix accurately.
Geometry: one compact floating white shell, inset from page edges, continuous iOS app-icon corner curves around all four exterior corners, soft diffused shadow. Target 48 CSS pixels high at a 1440-pixel desktop viewport. Do not make a tall toolbar. No pale blue or pink sections inside.
In top header, full Software logo on the left at a modest 250-pixel CSS width; local links Products, Open Source, Agents & Skills across the central zone, then EN / DE. Keep navigation and language grouped with the current site. After generous separation and a tiny neutral hairline, a small simple text link “Our agency ↗” sits at the far right. This is plain medium-size graphite sans-serif text, not stylized as a branded lockup. A tiny berry arrow is its sole sibling accent.
Bottom header mirrors the same layout: full Consulting logo, Services, Profiles, References, EN / DE, and a small plain text link “Our software ↗” at the far right, with a tiny teal arrow.
Under the top header, one restrained regular serif page line reads “Products, open source and agent tools.” Under the lower header, “Architecture and engineering for complex web applications.” Those are body-context samples, not massive hero headlines.
Constraints: no second logo in either header. No text Sebastian/Consulting in the Software header, no text Sebastian/Software in the Consulting header. Sibling link must look like a way out, current logo like the host. Arrow outward, not a dropdown chevron. No pill of a competing pastel brand. Native high-resolution crisp raster.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Edit target: the attached two-state desktop header sheet.
Change only scale and utility-link hierarchy. Keep the two states, their exact current logos with full Sebastian/slash/suffix, exact local links, context lines, all colors, white shell, smooth corners and shadow. Each row must still have exactly one logo; do not add the other logo.
The header shell is currently far too tall. Reduce BOTH toolbar heights to exactly HALF their current height, approximately 60 raster pixels on this same 1814-pixel-wide sheet. Scale each complete logo proportionally down to approximately 300 raster pixels wide and 50 raster pixels high; retain the full uncropped lockup. Shrink local nav and language to 20 raster pixels, with centered vertical alignment and generous horizontal spacing.
Make the external “Our agency ↗” and “Our software ↗” visibly secondary: 17 raster pixels, graphite sans-serif, with a small outward arrow, in a small very light neutral-gray utility capsule at the far-right end inside the enclosing shell. Keep at least 45 raster pixels of separation between the current language and this external capsule. It must look like a utility destination, not another local navigation item or second masthead. No pastel tint and no logo in this capsule.
Do not alter the page context sentences beneath either header. Preserve the canvas and blank page around them. Native crisp high-resolution raster.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Style: polished desktop website design, refined editorial magazine typography, quiet rigorous grid, unusually generous vertical breathing room. New serif typography must use regular/book weight; source logo typography stays faithful. Canvas white, graphite body text, subtle paper grain, no browser chrome, no viewport frame. Avoid pastel pink and pale blue fields, avoid duplicate brand emblems, avoid slogan clutter, oversized headings, full-page dark blocks, photos, city maps, phones and table views. Create a fresh composition, not a rearrangement of the earlier twin-logo design.
Asset type: one complete desktop page-ending study, landscape-to-square composition approximately 1440 x 1440, with three separate sections in this exact order: shared Newsletter, editorial invitation to the other website, actual current-site footer.
Primary request: completely rethink the brand hierarchy. This is the Software website. The current site is the publisher with one substantial original logo in its footer; the other site is an outward editorial invitation without any logo or pinwheel emblem. No stacked pair of logos. Make HERE versus THERE differ in composition, typography, scale and role.
Input image: original current-site Sebastian/Software logo as brand artwork reference, not as layout reference. Preserve the whole source emblem and Sebastian/slash/suffix, shapes, proportions and source colors; do not invent a replacement wordmark.
SECTION 1: a quiet narrow Newsletter passage on white, with a normal 28px regular serif heading “Newsletter”, description “Insights into our work across software and consulting: what we're building, exploring and thinking about.” Compact Email address field and Subscribe button to the right. Shared graphite/neutral design, no brand logo. Comfortable 72px top/bottom margins. Newsletter should not dominate the page.
SECTION 2: a generous unboxed editorial destination on white, asymmetrical two-column spread with a restrained 38px regular-serif question on the left, body explanation below it and a simple underlined outward link. This section has NO logo, NO emblem and NO wordmark treatment. Large calm whitespace separates it from both neighboring sections. To the right, one small bespoke graphite-and-berry line illustration occupying no more than one fifth of the entire page width, with an understated diagonal corner detail. It must read as a related story, NOT a second footer or a partner branding panel.
Exact question: “Need a clearer direction for your software?”
Exact description: “Our agency helps teams with software architecture, engineering and technical direction.”
Exact action in plain sans-serif: “Meet Sebastian/Consulting ↗”
Illustration: a thin technical pencil drawing of a trail through an abstract terrain, with several considered routes and a small moving destination marker, selective muted berry accent. Delicate, spacious, not a giant icon or pinwheel.
SECTION 3: the actual current-site footer is a substantial inset floating panel on very light neutral gray, subtly textured, softly rounded continuous exterior corners, faint shadow, approximately 64px side insets; NOT edge-to-edge. Big enough to feel like the page's own closing masthead. Display the complete original Software teal lockup ONLY HERE, about 400 CSS px wide on the left. No other brand logo anywhere in the whole image. To its right, a neatly aligned current-site link column: Products / Open Source / Agents & Skills / Company / Journal. Below the logo, an uncluttered legal company/address block in small sans-serif: “Sebastian Software GmbH”, “Dalheimer Straße 12”, “55128 Mainz”, “Germany”, “info@sebastian-software.de”. On the right lower side, small single-color outline social UI glyphs labeled LinkedIn and GitHub, both in the current site's text ink. No colorful platform logos. At the bottom, one thin quiet legal row “© 2026 Sebastian Software GmbH” and links “Imprint”, “Privacy”, “Contact”.
Visual hierarchy: small utility newsletter → open editorial outward story → substantial clearly owned footer masthead. Three areas must look materially different, NOT three identical horizontal cards, and their content must breathe vertically. Actual footer has only local navigation, registered address, legal and social links. Sibling brand name appears only as plain text inside the editorial action. No NEWSLETTER inside the actual footer. Native high-resolution raster, exact readable text.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Edit target: the attached complete software desktop page ending.
Change only typography scale, vertical breathing room and social glyph rendering. Keep the established three-section order, exact copy, original complete current-site logo, registered address, local/legal/social link labels, neutral footer shell, shadow, colors and the existing single illustration. Exactly ONE brand logo in the whole page. Never add a sibling logo.
The editorial invitation headline is currently too large/heavy. Re-render it at approximately 38 raster pixels, LIGHT REGULAR/BOOK serif weight (400), airy 1.25 line height; do not use bold or semibold. Let it wrap into two lines if needed. Re-render its body at 21 raster pixels, regular serif, 1.45 line height; outward action at 19 raster pixels plain sans-serif. Keep the source logo's weights and shapes unchanged.
Newsletter heading 29 raster pixels regular serif, copy 18 raster pixels regular sans-serif with 1.5 line height. Form remains compact and horizontally aligned.
Remove the divider line beneath Newsletter. Use approximately 115 raster pixels of clear white vertical separation before the invitation and approximately 95 raster pixels after the invitation before the footer panel. Preserve the page's airy proportions and current/footer prominence. Slightly reduce the illustration if needed so it does not dominate the more restrained headline. Do not compress the canvas to remove the newly freed space.
Social glyphs: keep labels LinkedIn and GitHub, replace the large platform silhouettes with two matching tiny 16px single-color monoline interface glyphs. Same stroke thickness and text ink, no filled brand tile or official colorful platform logo.
Preserve all spellings and original wordmark proportions. Native crisp high-resolution raster.
